# Model Documentation and Validation Report

**Model suite:** retail credit risk PD / LGD / EAD with an IFRS 9 expected credit loss engine
**Reporting date:** 2018-12-31
**Data basis:** synthetic book of 120,000 loans, seed 42 (`data_mode=synthetic`)
**Generated by:** `python scripts/run_pipeline.py` — every figure in this document is reproducible from that command

> This is a *model validation report* in structure and intent. It is what a bank's second-line model
> risk function produces, and it is deliberately written to expose weaknesses rather than defend the
> model. Where a number is a policy choice, it is labelled as one.

---

## 1. Model inventory

| ID | Model | Purpose | Method | Selected for use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | PD scorecard | Rank and score applications; produce 12-month PD | WOE-transformed logistic regression, points scaling | **Yes** |
| M2 | PD challenger | Benchmark M1's discrimination | LightGBM on raw features, frozen category encoding | No — benchmark only |
| M3 | Calibrator | Convert M1's output into usable PD levels | Isotonic regression, fitted on 2016, frozen | **Yes** |
| M4 | LGD model | Loss given default per loan | Gradient boosting on workout loss, floored/capped | **Yes** (beat benchmark by 41.4% MAE) |
| M5 | EAD model | Exposure at default | Per-grade default timing × contractual amortisation | **Yes** |
| M6 | ECL engine | IFRS 9 provision | Three-stage, discounted, probability-weighted scenarios | **Yes** |

## 2. Data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Loans | 120,000 |
| Resolved (Fully Paid / Charged Off) | 97,277 |
| Train 2013–2015 | 40,633 — 12-month default rate 3.03% |
| Test 2016 | 18,720 — 2.86% |
| Out-of-time 2017 | 21,792 — 2.48% |
| Open book at 2018-12-31 | 22,723 — exposure 314,598,257 |
| Defaulted loans used for LGD training | 6,047 |
| Defaulted loans used for LGD/EAD validation | 5,199 |

**Split discipline.** The split is chronological. Random splits on credit data leak macro conditions
across the split and overstate performance, which is why the pipeline cannot produce one.

**Censoring.** Recent vintages contain unresolved loans. They are excluded from PD training — the
outcome is unobservable, not zero — and they form the open book that the ECL engine provisions
against. Censoring is applied independently of the outcome, so the resolved sample is unbiased.

**Excluded inputs.** `config.LEAKAGE_COLUMNS` lists every post-origination column (repayment totals,
recoveries, outstanding balance, days past due, outcome). A unit test asserts the feature set and
the leakage set are disjoint, so the guard cannot be removed by accident.

## 3. Validation results

### 3.1 Discrimination (out-of-time, 2017)

| Model | AUC | 95% bootstrap CI | Gini | KS | Brier |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| M1+M3 scorecard, calibrated | 0.7592 | 0.7418 – 0.7760 | 0.5183 | 0.3841 | 0.02368 |
| M2 LightGBM challenger | 0.7281 | – | 0.4561 | 0.3441 | 0.02411 |

**Finding:** the interpretable scorecard outperforms the boosted challenger. The internal risk grade
is the dominant driver and is close to monotonic in risk, so the linear binned specification captures
most of the available signal. There is no discrimination argument in this book for deploying an
unexplainable model.

### 3.2 Calibration (out-of-time)

Isotonic calibration was fitted on 2016 and frozen before application to 2017. Predicted versus
observed default rate by decile is exported to `outputs/tables/calibration_calibrated_oot.csv`, and
the calibration curve is `outputs/figures/calibration.png`.

**Why calibration was necessary:** on this book the uncalibrated scorecard ranks well but its PD
levels are not usable in a provision calculation without correction. Discrimination and calibration
are separate problems and passing the first does not imply the second.

### 3.3 Stability

| Measure | Value | Band |
|---|---:|---|
| Score PSI, train vs test | 0.0044 | stable |
| Score PSI, train vs out-of-time | 0.0360 | stable |
| Highest feature PSI, train vs out-of-time | 0.0490 | stable |

PSI is computed on WOE-transformed feature distributions and on the score. Bands: `< 0.10` stable,
`0.10 – 0.25` monitor, `> 0.25` material shift / redevelop.

### 3.4 LGD model validation

| Basis | MAE | R² | Mean predicted / observed |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| M4 modeled LGD | **0.0239** | **0.824** | 0.8905 / 0.8947 |
| Grade-average lookup | 0.0408 | 0.473 | 0.8938 / 0.8947 |

**Conclusion:** the model beats the incumbent by 41.4% on MAE and is retained. The selection is
automatic: had the model failed this test, the base provision would have used the lookup table and
this document would say so.

### 3.5 EAD model validation

| Measure | Value |
|---|---:|
| Observed mean exposure ratio at default | 0.5280 |
| Predicted mean exposure ratio | 0.5866 |
| Per-loan MAE (exposure ratio) | 0.2245 |

**Interpretation, stated because it is easy to misread:** the model predicts the conditional mean
exposure, so per-loan error is bounded below by the variance of realised default timing — a large
per-loan MAE is expected and is not evidence of a poor model. What matters is the mean (overstated by
5.9 percentage points, i.e. conservative for provisioning) and the ranking by grade. The residual
mean overstatement is attributed to smoothing of the timing distribution in the tail months and to
using a training-vintage timing profile on later vintages; it is conservative, and it is a known bias
rather than an unexplained one.

## 4. Assumption register

Every assumption below is a *choice*. Each one is recorded with its basis and its sensitivity so that
a reviewer can challenge it rather than discover it.

| # | Assumption | Value | Basis | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Default definition | Charged Off within 12 months of origination | Keeps PD and the ECL horizon on one clock | Material — a lifetime definition compounds the provision |
| A2 | Max lifetime horizon | 60 months | Contractual term | Low — bounded by the amortisation schedule |
| A3 | LGD floor / cap | 0.45 / 0.95 | Stabilises thin samples | Moderate |
| A4 | Discount rate | max(contract rate, 5%) | Proxy for the effective interest rate | Low at current rate levels |
| A5 | SICR PD threshold | 6.0% | Policy; set above normal portfolio PD so Stage 2 is genuine deterioration | **High — ±35% of ECL across the tested range** |
| A6 | SICR backstop | 30+ days past due | Required by the standard | Low |
| A7 | Stage 3 trigger | 90+ days past due | Standard credit-impaired definition | Low |
| A8 | Scenario set | optimistic −1.5pp, base 0, adverse +2.0pp, severe +4.5pp | Policy | High |
| A9 | Scenario weights | 10 / 50 / 28 / 12 % | Policy, base-dominated | High |
| A10 | PD–unemployment elasticity | 0.15, `PD_mult = exp(0.15 ΔU)` | **Illustrative, not estimated** | High — see limitation L3 |
| A11 | 50:50 and employer checks | n/a for modelling | — | Not modelled |

### 4.1 The disclosure that matters most

| SICR PD threshold | Stage 2 share | Total ECL | vs selected |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3.0% | 27.1% | 7,836,557 | +14.1% |
| 4.5% | 14.2% | 7,012,341 | +2.1% |
| **6.0% (selected)** | **12.5%** | **6,869,152** | **0.0%** |
| 8.0% | 5.1% | 6,025,115 | −12.3% |
| 12.0% | 1.8% | 5,459,576 | −20.5% |

A single policy threshold moves the provision by more than a third across a plausible range. Any
statement of "the provision is X" without this table is incomplete.

## 5. Known limitations

| ID | Limitation | Effect | Mitigation / next step |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Synthetic book by default | Absolute levels are not market results; pipeline structure is the deliverable | `make pipeline-real` on a LendingClub extract |
| L2 | No time-varying covariates | SICR cannot reflect true PD migration since origination; Stage 2 is driven by delinquency and absolute PD | Monthly behavioural scoring on bureau data |
| L3 | Macro overlay is an elasticity, not a satellite model | Scenario ECL magnitudes are indicative | Fit a satellite regression on a long default-rate history |
| L4 | LGD has no cure / re-default process | LGD slightly understated for restructured exposures | Multi-state workout model |
| L5 | EAD ignores prepayment | ECL overstated, since prepayment removes exposure | Add a prepayment model alongside EAD |
| L6 | Single reporting date | No backtest of staging transitions | Roll the engine monthly and compare stage migration to realised transitions |
| L7 | Costs in the cut-off analysis are assumed | The optimal cut-off is only as good as the 1.0 : 0.05 cost ratio | Calibrate costs from realised margin and loss data |

## 6. Monitoring plan

| Trigger | Threshold | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Score PSI vs training | > 0.10 monitor, > 0.25 act | Investigate population drift; redevelop if persistent |
| Feature PSI | > 0.25 on any input | Review that feature's binning |
| Gini deterioration | > 20% relative fall vs validation | Recalibrate or redevelop |
| Calibration drift | Observed / predicted ratio outside 0.8 – 1.25 | Recalibrate PD levels |
| Stage migration | Actual stage 2/3 transition rates vs projected | Re-examine SICR policy (A5) |
| LGD benchmark gap | Model MAE no longer below the lookup table | Revert to the lookup table — the selection is automatic, not permanent |

## 7. Validation conclusion

The suite is **fit for the stated purpose** — demonstrating an auditable PD → LGD → EAD → ECL chain
on a retail book — subject to four conditions, all of which are disclosure rather than defect:

1. The synthetic book must be disclosed wherever its numbers are quoted. **Done** in the README and
   in `outputs/RESULTS.md`.
2. The provision must always be presented with the SICR sensitivity table (A5). **Done** in §4.1.
3. The macro overlay must be labelled illustrative until a satellite model replaces it (A10, L3).
   **Done** in §4 and in the README limitations.
4. The EAD model must be judged on the mean and by grade, not on per-loan MAE (§3.5). **Done**.

**Weaknesses that would block production deployment, in priority order:** the macro overlay (A10),
time-varying covariates (L2), prepayment (L5).

## 8. Reproduce

```bash
make setup
make pipeline      # regenerates outputs/figures, outputs/tables, outputs/metrics.json, outputs/RESULTS.md
make test          # 60 tests, including the leakage guard and the ECL staging logic
```

`outputs/RESULTS.md` is generated by the same objects that produced the figures, so a number cannot
appear in this document or in the README that the pipeline did not calculate.
